Governance Workflow

Source: vignettes/governance-workflow.Rmd
governance-workflow.Rmd
library( governance )
library( dplyr )
library( ggplot2 )

theme_set( theme_minimal() )

This article walks through the path from raw 990 fields to governance scores and explains each column the package adds. It uses the bundled dat_example, a 5,000-organization sample of raw 2022 fields. In practice the data come from get_governance_data(); see vignette("download-data").

data( "dat_example", package = "governance" )

set.seed( 57 )
rows        <- sample( nrow(dat_example), 1000 )
dat_example <- dat_example[ rows, ]

Step 1: Code the practice items

get_features() returns the input with three groups of columns appended.

Columns What they are Used by
16 GI_* items Recommended practices, 1 = present the 2023 index (default)
5 RISK_* indicators Reported risk events or exposures, 1 = reported not scored; reported alongside
12 P*_LINE_* features Features of the 2018 model get_scores( model = "legacy-2018" ) 
features <- get_features( dat_example )

Practice items

Each GI_* item records one practice. A blank answer is NA, not 0, and the scoring model uses whichever items an organization answered.

Item Form 990 line Practice
GI_REVIEW_AUDIT XII-2a/2b, IV-12a/b Financial statements compiled, reviewed or audited
GI_AUDIT XII-2b, IV-12a/b Financial statements audited by an independent accountant
GI_AUDIT_CMTE XII-2c A committee oversees the audit or review (0 if no review or audit)
GI_ACCRUAL XII-1 Accrual accounting
GI_INDEP_MAJOR VI-1a/1b At least half of voting members are independent
GI_MINUTES_BOARD VI-8a Board meetings documented
GI_MINUTES_CMTE VI-8b Committee meetings documented
GI_990_BOARD VI-11a Form 990 given to the board before filing
GI_COI VI-12a Written conflict-of-interest policy
GI_COI_DISCLOSE VI-12b Annual disclosure of interests (0 without a policy)
GI_COI_MONITOR VI-12c Policy monitored and enforced (0 without a policy)
GI_WHISTLE VI-13 Written whistleblower policy
GI_RETENTION VI-14 Written document retention and destruction policy
GI_COMP_CEO VI-15a Independent pay-setting process for the top executive
GI_COMP_OTH VI-15b Independent pay-setting process for other officers
GI_990_WEB VI-18 Form 990 posted on the organization’s own website

Practices differ a great deal in how common they are. Nearly every filer documents board meetings; fewer than one in ten posts its 990 online.

rates <-
  features |>
  summarise( across(starts_with("GI_"), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer( everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "share" )

ggplot( rates, aes(x = share, y = reorder(item, share)) ) +
  geom_col( fill = "#1696d2" ) +
  scale_x_continuous( labels = scales::percent ) +
  labs( x = "Share of organizations reporting the practice", y = NULL )

Risk indicators

The RISK_* columns record events that good governance is meant to manage: business transactions with insiders (IV-28a/b/c), loans to insiders (IV-26), family or business ties among officers (VI-2), use of a management company (VI-3) and asset diversions (VI-5). They are not part of the index. They are disclosures, not practices, and they rise with organization size, so they correlate positively with good practice. Report them alongside the score.

features |>
  summarise( across(starts_with("RISK_"), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer( everything(), names_to = "indicator", values_to = "share" ) |>
  knitr::kable( digits = 3 )
indicator share
RISK_INSIDER_BIZ 0.053
RISK_LOAN 0.024
RISK_FAM_TIES 0.136
RISK_MGMT_CO 0.058
RISK_DIVERSION 0.001

Step 2: Calculate the scores 

scores <- get_scores( features )

get_scores() appends eight columns.

Column Meaning
gov_score General governance score. 0 is the average 2023 filer; one unit is one SD of the latent factor among 2023 filers.
gov_score_se Standard error of gov_score.
gov_s_finance Financial-assurance specific factor (audit, review, audit committee, accrual).
gov_s_minutes Minutes specific factor (board and committee minutes).
gov_s_policy Written-policies specific factor (conflict of interest, whistleblower, retention). Not recommended; see below.
gov_s_comp Compensation specific factor (CEO and other-officer pay process).
gov_count Number of the 16 practices reported (0–16).
gov_n_items Number of the 16 items answered.

The specific factors are residuals. They are uncorrelated with gov_score, and a positive value means the organization does more in that area than its general score predicts. They are not standalone subscales: an organization with a high gov_s_finance and a low gov_score is one that is audited but has few other practices.

The specific factors are also much less reliable than gov_score. Among 2023 filers the empirical reliability of the scores is:

Score Reliability Use
gov_score .83 Main score.
gov_s_finance .57 The one subscore with substantial variance of its own; report it alongside gov_score.
gov_s_comp .48 Supplementary (two items).
gov_s_minutes .41 Supplementary (two items).
gov_s_policy .29 Do not use.

Do not use gov_s_policy. The written-policy items are the core of gov_score, so the policy factor has almost no variance of its own (omega-hierarchical < .01). Its loadings only contrast the conflict-of-interest items with the whistleblower and retention policies. The column is returned for completeness. For simple domain-level measures, use the share of practices adopted in each domain instead. Those shares are not residuals, so they move with gov_score.

ggplot( scores, aes(x = gov_score) ) +
  geom_histogram( bins = 30, fill = "#1696d2" ) +
  labs( x = "Governance score", y = "Organizations" )

Score or count?

gov_count is a transparent alternative: the number of practices reported. It correlates about .96 with gov_score. The model-based score adds three things: practices are weighted by how much they reveal about governance, every score has a standard error, and the scale is anchored to 2023 so it does not drift as practices spread.

ggplot( scores, aes(x = gov_count, y = gov_score) ) +
  geom_jitter( width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3 ) +
  labs( x = "Practices reported (gov_count)", y = "gov_score" )

The vertical spread at each count shows the weighting at work. Two organizations that report eight practices can differ by a full unit, depending on which eight.

Precision

Scores are least precise at the ends of the scale, where few items discriminate. Treat differences smaller than about two standard errors as noise, especially at the top and bottom.

scores |>
  mutate( quintile = ntile(gov_score, 5) ) |>
  group_by( quintile ) |>
  summarise( mean_score = mean(gov_score), mean_se = mean(gov_score_se) ) |>
  knitr::kable( digits = 2 )
quintile mean_score mean_se
1 -1.27 0.51
2 -0.72 0.30
3 -0.08 0.19
4 0.50 0.30
5 1.14 0.53

Missing answers

Rows with blank answers are still scored from the items they did answer; their standard errors are larger. Rows that answered none of the 16 items get NA scores.

table( items_answered = scores$gov_n_items ) |>
  knitr::kable( col.names = c("Items answered", "Organizations") )
Items answered Organizations
14 1
15 22
16 977

Comparing organizations

Size is the strongest predictor of almost every practice, partly because audits are required above state and federal thresholds. Compare organizations of similar size, or adjust for size in a model. vignette("overview") shows the size gradient across the whole sector.

To relate scores to size, sector or location, join them to the NCCS Business Master File on ORG_EIN. The snippet below is not run here because it downloads a large file.

bmf_url <- paste0( "https://nccsdata.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/",
                   "bmf/unified/v1.2/UNIFIED_BMF_V1.2.csv" )

bmf     <- readr::read_csv( bmf_url )
bmf$EIN <- stringr::str_pad( gsub("\\D", "", bmf$EIN), 9, pad = "0" )

joined <- left_join( scores, bmf, by = c("ORG_EIN" = "EIN") )

The legacy 2018 model

Earlier versions of the package scored organizations with a six-factor model fit to 2018 data. It is kept for reproducing earlier work, but it has known problems, including negative weights on several good practices. See vignette("legacy-2018-model").

legacy <- get_scores( features, model = "legacy-2018" )
